s1.syndrome_frame: Neonatal presentation with respiratory distress, feeding difficulties, and hypotonia, with a complex congenital cardiac anomaly and maternal history of cardiac anomalies
salient_findings: Difficulty swallowing with choking and excessive oral secretions
PDA, patent foramen ovale, widened coronary sinus, permanent left superior vena cava and pericardial effusion
High forehead and small lower jaw
key_facts: Female neonate born at 37+6 weeks gestation
NICU transfer due to low oxygen saturation
Mother's history of strabismus, cataract, and cardiac anomalies
PDA, patent foramen ovale, widened coronary sinus, permanent left superior vena cava and pericardial effusion
Mildly elevated WBC count in CSF initially
Cranial CT + enhancement shows slightly hypointense shadows
Follow-up EEG shows increased amplitude of all-conductor waves with scattered spikes
Fiber-optic bronchoscopy shows pronounced swelling in bilateral arytenoid epiglottis folds
Heterozygous variant in ATAD3A gene (c.1517A>C; p.Q506P)

shortlist.label: CHARGE syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Respiratory distress, feeding difficulties, hypotonia, and congenital cardiac anomalies match key features of CHARGE syndrome

shortlist.label: Pierre Robin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Laryngeal stridor, difficulty swallowing, and small lower jaw are consistent with Pierre Robin syndrome

shortlist.label: VACTERL association
shortlist.why_kept: Complex congenital cardiac anomalies, respiratory distress, and feeding difficulties are seen in VACTERL association

shortlist.label: DiGeorge syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Congenital cardiac anomalies, hypotonia, and hypocalcemia (not explicitly mentioned but possible) are features of DiGeorge syndrome

shortlist.label: Mowat-Wilson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous variant in ATAD3A gene and clinical features such as hypotonia, congenital cardiac anomalies, and developmental delays are consistent with Mowat-Wilson syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of laryngeal stridor, difficulty swallowing, hypotonia, and specific cardiac anomalies such as PDA, along with the mother's history of strabismus and cataract, points towards CHARGE syndrome, which is characterized by Coloboma, Heart defects, Atresia of the choanae, Restricted growth and development, Genital abnormalities, and Ear anomalies. The heterozygous variant in the ATAD3A gene also supports this diagnosis, although it is more commonly associated with Harel-Yoon syndrome, the combination of clinical features presented aligns more closely with CHARGE syndrome.

rejected.label: Pierre Robin syndrome
rejected.why: Primarily involves micrognathia and glossoptosis, not fully explained by the provided clinical features

rejected.label: VACTERL association
rejected.why: Involves vertebral defects, anal atresia, cardiac defects, tracheoesophageal fistula, renal anomalies, and limb abnormalities, which are not all present in this case

rejected.label: DiGeorge syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by thymic hypoplasia, parathyroid gland abnormalities, and cardiac defects, but the specific constellation of features in this case does not align closely with DiGeorge syndrome

rejected.label: Mowat-Wilson syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by distinctive facial features, intellectual disability, and variable systemic anomalies, but the specific features and genetic findings in this case do not align with Mowat-Wilson syndrome

gold: Harel-Yoon syndrome (HAYOS) caused by ATAD3A gene mutation
